unit.title: Perform oxyacetylene welding process (fuel gas) to AWS specification

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A client's drawing says a small-bore steel line must be gas welded 'to the AWS code the Centre uses'. Which document should the welder work from at the bench?
options: The torch maker's lighting card
The gas supplier's delivery note
The client's order and invoice
The WPS written for that joint

questions.stem: Which set of details would you expect to find on a WPS for oxy-fuel gas welding (OFW) of carbon steel?
options: Electrode class, current, polarity and shielding gas
Wire feed speed, voltage and stick-out length
Grit size, disc speed and grinding angle
Base metal, rod class, nozzle size, flame and position

questions.stem: Why does an OFW procedure state the flame type (for example, neutral) as well as the nozzle size?
options: The flame type sets the colour of the finished cap
A wrong flame adds carbon or oxygen to the weld
The flame type tells the inspector how fast to work
Only a carburising flame will melt carbon steel

questions.stem: During a procedure qualification test, a recorder writes down the nozzle size, rod class, pressures and position that were really used. Where do these real values go?
options: On the welder's time sheet for the week
On the gas supplier's cylinder label
On the PQR (procedure qualification record)
On the client's purchase order for the job's steel

questions.stem: Shanice passes an OFW test on carbon steel plate in the vertical (3G) position. Under most AWS codes, which statement about her qualification is true?
options: It covers every welding process, including MMAW
It covers every metal, including aluminium
It lasts for life, whatever work she does
It covers a set range of thickness and positions

questions.stem: A welder wants to fusion weld a steel coupon with an oxy-propane flame instead of oxy-acetylene, to save money. Why is this a poor idea?
options: Propane flame is not hot or concentrated enough
Propane cylinders cannot be fitted with regulators
Propane leaves a hard, glassy slag on the weld
Propane can only be used with a carburising flame

questions.stem: During a qualification test, the assessor finds that a trainee's 3G coupon was welded lying flat on the bench. What should the assessor do?
options: Reject the test, as the position was not as set
Accept it, as flat welding is harder to do well
Accept it, if the bend tests later pass
Ask another trainee to sign that it was vertical

questions.stem: A trainee feels the closed test bay is stuffy and opens the oxygen valve on his torch to 'freshen the air'. Why is this dangerous?
options: Oxygen makes the air too cold to breathe
Oxygen puts out the flames of other torches
Oxygen turns the steel coupons rusty at once
Oxygen-rich air makes clothes burn fiercely

questions.stem: An acetylene cylinder for the test bay was carried lying flat in a van. Why must it stand upright for a time before it is used?
options: So the gas inside can warm up to room heat
So acetone settles and is not drawn out
So the valve can be checked for oil and grit
So the paint on the cylinder can dry

questions.stem: The WPS gives a nozzle size, but the Centre's torches come from a different maker with a different numbering. What should the welder do?
options: Use the maker's chart to find the matching nozzle
Use the nozzle that looks the closest in size
Use the largest nozzle to be sure of fusion
Drill out a small nozzle to the size needed

questions.stem: In the AWS gas welding rod class R60, what does the number 60 mainly tell you?
options: The rod length, in centimetres
The flame temperature needed, in tens of degrees
The rod's carbon content, in hundredths of a per cent
The weld metal's least tensile strength, in ksi

questions.stem: Why are copper-coated steel gas welding rods kept dry and clean in their tube until they are used?
options: Rust and dirt on the rod can cause porosity
Damp rods give an electric shock to the welder
Clean rods need no flame to melt them
The copper coat falls off if it gets warm

questions.stem: Which filler rod diameter is usually a sound choice for an OFW butt joint in 3 mm carbon steel plate, if the WPS allows it?
options: About 1.0 mm
About 5.0 mm
About 6.0 mm
About 2.4 mm

questions.stem: Part-way through a test weld, a small white feather appears beyond the inner cone of a neutral flame. What has happened, and what should the welder do?
options: It has become oxidising; add more acetylene
It has become carburising; add a little oxygen
It is now at its hottest; carry on just as it is
The nozzle is blocked; turn both gases up

questions.stem: What does an oxidising flame (too much oxygen) usually do to the weld metal on carbon steel?
options: It makes the weld smooth, bright and tough
It adds carbon, so the weld becomes hard
It burns the metal, giving sparks and porosity
It slows the weld down, so the HAZ is narrow

questions.stem: A WPS calls for a square butt with a gap on 3 mm plate, but a single-V preparation on 6 mm plate. Why?
options: A V is needed so the rod can be held still
Thick plate does not need any root gap
Without a V, the flame cannot fuse the full depth
Square edges on thick plate always crack as they cool

questions.stem: Plate coupons for an OFW test have mill scale along the edges and faces. What should be done before tacking?
options: Grind or file the joint area to bright metal
Leave the scale on, as it acts as a flux
Paint the edges so they do not rust
Heat the scale red so it burns off in the weld

questions.stem: Two coupon plates are tacked for a 3G test. Why should each tack be small and fully fused?
options: Big tacks make the coupon too heavy to lift
Big or cold tacks leave lumps and poor fusion
Small tacks need no cleaning at all
The assessor only counts the number of tacks

questions.stem: Which AWS position matches the ISO position PF (vertical up) for a butt weld in plate?
options: 1G
2G
4G
3G

questions.stem: A welder passes a 6G test on small-bore carbon steel pipe with OFW. Generally, which positions does this cover?
options: Only the 45° fixed position he tested in
Flat and horizontal positions only, on plate or pipe
All positions, within the limits the code sets
Overhead only, as that part was the hardest

questions.stem: On a 6G pipe coupon, which part of the joint is usually the hardest for a gas welder to keep fully fused at the root?
options: The top, where the weld is flat
The sides, where the weld is vertical
The bottom, where the weld is overhead
Every part is the same, as the pipe is fixed

questions.stem: Why is backhand (rightward) technique often named in a WPS for gas welding pipe or plate thicker than about 6 mm?
options: It fuses deeper with a narrower V
It needs no filler rod at all
It works only with an oxidising flame
It lets the welder skip the tack welds

questions.stem: During a test weld the inner cone keeps touching the molten pool. What is this most likely to cause?
options: A cleaner pool with deeper fusion
A cooler flame and a narrow HAZ
No effect, as long as the rod is clean
Popping, backfires and a dirty pool

questions.stem: Why should the hot end of the filler rod be kept inside the flame's outer envelope while welding?
options: So it stays shielded from the air
So it cools quickly between dips
So it can be used to stir the pool
So the flame turns carburising

questions.stem: A welder stops part-way round a pipe coupon to pick up a new rod. How should he restart?
options: Start a new pool just beside the old one
Reheat the end of the weld and fuse back into it
Add rod first, then bring the flame in
Leave a gap and fill it in at the very end

questions.stem: Why are the pipe ends for an OFW test coupon cleaned on the inside as well as the outside before fit-up?
options: So the root can fuse cleanly on the inside wall
So the assessor can read the pipe markings
So the pipe weighs less on the stand
So no tack welds are needed anywhere on the joint

questions.stem: For a welder test on plate under the AWS code the Centre uses, which tests are most often used on an OFW groove weld?
options: A hardness test on the cap only
A paint adhesion test on the face
Visual inspection, then face and root bends
A pressure test with compressed air in the shop

questions.stem: To qualify a PROCEDURE (not just a welder) on plate, which test is normally added to the bend tests?
options: Tensile tests across the weld
A spark test on the filler rod
A leak test on the gas hoses
A colour check of the flame

questions.stem: Why are bend strips from an OFW coupon cut by saw or machine, and not by flame cutting close to the weld?
options: Flame cutting heats and changes the metal
Saw cuts make the strip bend more easily
Flame cutting is not allowed on carbon steel
Saw cuts hide small faults on the edges

questions.stem: A root bend strip shows one open defect 1 mm long. For this test, the code the Centre uses allows open defects up to 3 mm. What is the result for that strip?
options: It fails, as any defect at all is a fail
It must be bent again the other way
It is judged on the cap side only
It passes, as the defect is within the limit

questions.stem: On a fixed pipe coupon, why are the bend strips taken from places the code sets round the pipe, and not where the welder chooses?
options: So the strips are easier to cut out
So the hardest positions are always tested
So the welder can pick his best section
So fewer strips are needed in total

questions.stem: Visual inspection of a 3G coupon finds incomplete fusion along the root on the back of the plate. What is the usual result?
options: The coupon fails and is not bend tested
The root is filled from the back, then tested
It passes if the cap looks good
Only the cap is ground off and re-welded

questions.stem: Why is the back (root side) of each gas-welded plate coupon inspected as well as the face?
options: The root side shows the welder's speed
The root shows if penetration is full and even
The root side is where the cap is measured
The code only allows the back to be painted

questions.stem: A trainee's gas weld coupon shows a small star-shaped crack in the hollow at the very end of the run. What should he do differently next time?
options: Turn the flame up just before he stops
Stop quickly by pulling the flame straight off
Fill the crater and lift the flame slowly
Quench the end of the weld in water at once

questions.stem: The code limits misalignment (hi-lo) between the two plates of a butt coupon. Why?
options: A step at the root stops full fusion and adds stress
A step makes the coupon harder to stamp
Misaligned plates use too much gas
The bend jig will not hold a misaligned strip

questions.stem: After a welder passes an OFW test, which details must the WPQ (welder performance qualification) record show?
options: His home address and next of kin only
The price of the gas and rods used
Process, positions, metal, thickness range, results
The make of torch, nozzle and the colour of the hoses

questions.stem: Why does a gas welder's continuity log matter for keeping his OFW qualification in force?
options: It records how much gas he uses
It shows he has used the process within the set time
It lists every customer and job he has worked on this year
It proves he has bought his own goggles

questions.stem: Each test coupon gives 3 bend strips, and 1 spare is cut from each coupon as well. Seven trainees each weld one plate coupon. How many strips must be cut?
One pass on a plate coupon takes 6 minutes. Nine coupons each need one pass. How many hours of welding is that?
options: 0.6 hours
0.9 hours
1.5 hours
5.4 hours

questions.stem: Each torch uses about 200 litres of acetylene an hour. Three torches are used for 4.5 hours on a test day. About how much acetylene is used?
options: 900 litres
1 350 litres
3 600 litres
2 700 litres

questions.stem: A trainee's 3G coupon fails the root bend. He asks to cut a new strip from the same coupon 'from a better part'. What should the team leader do?
options: Let him choose a new strip from the best part
Pass him anyway, as the face bend was good
Follow the code's retest rules; no picking strips
Fail him for life from all gas welding tests

questions.stem: You run an OFW test day for five trainees. What should you do before the first coupon is tacked?
options: Hand out rods and let them start when ready
Brief the WPS, check each set and issue marked coupons
Let the trainees choose their own nozzle sizes
Tell them the bend test results will be ignored

questions.stem: Your crew must gas weld small-bore steel air lines in a factory in Spanish Town to a WPS. A new welder has no OFW test record. What should you do?
options: Let him weld, as gas welding is simple
Let him weld the joints that are hard to see
Have him tested to the WPS before he welds
Ask him to sign a note saying he is qualified

questions.stem: Before a test session, the team leader checks each oxy-acetylene set. Where are flashback arrestors normally fitted for the best protection?
options: Inside the cylinder, under the valve
On the regulator outlets, with check valves at the torch
Only half-way along each hose
On the oxygen side only, never on the fuel gas side at all

questions.stem: After the bend tests, the coupons and broken strips are left on the bench. What should be done with them?
options: Throw them all in the scrap bin at once
Label and keep them with the test records
Give them to the trainees to take home
Weld them together to make a stand for the bay

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: In AWS terms, what do the letters OFW stand for?
What is the AWS position code for a pipe groove weld with the pipe fixed at 45° to the horizontal, and no restriction ring?
Which ISO position letters match the AWS 3G position welded uphill on plate?
In the AWS gas welding rod class R60, what does the letter R stand for?
A gas welder adjusts the flame until the white feather just disappears into the inner cone. What is this flame called?
In procedure qualification, what is the name of the test that pulls a strip cut across the weld until it breaks?
Each coupon gives 2 face bends and 2 root bends. Six coupons are tested. How many strips are bent in all?
What is the name of the bend test in which the cap side of the weld is on the outside of the bend?
What is the name of the record that shows a welder has used a process within the set time, so his qualification stays in force?
A WPS allows a root gap of 2 to 3 mm. The fitter measures 3.5 mm. By how many millimetres is the gap over the limit?
What is the name of the small, bright cone of flame right at the nozzle tip?
When a gas weld run ends without the pool being filled, a hollow is left. What is this hollow called?
What is the term for the step between the surfaces of two plates or pipes that are not lined up at the joint?
A coupon is 150 mm long and is welded at 50 mm per minute. How many minutes does one run take?
Which fuel gas is used with oxygen for fusion welding of steel, because it gives the hottest flame?

essays.stem: Explain the main details an OFW WPS for carbon steel must give, and why a welder must not change any of them without approval.
essays.modelAnswer: An OFW WPS gives the base metal and its thickness range, the joint design (square butt or single-V, the angle, root face and gap), and the filler rod class and size. It names the fuel gas, the flame type (neutral for carbon steel) and the nozzle size, using the maker's chart for pressures. It states the position or positions, the direction of travel and the technique (forehand or backhand), and any backing, preheat or cleaning between runs. Each detail was proved by the procedure test recorded on the PQR. If a welder changes one, such as a bigger nozzle, a different rod or another position, the weld may not have the strength or fusion that was proved. Some changes mean the procedure must be qualified again. So any change must be approved by the person in charge, and recorded, before welding.
markingPoints: Base metal, thickness range and joint design
Filler rod class and size
Fuel gas, flame type and nozzle size
Position, technique and direction of travel
Changes may void the proved procedure; approval and record needed

essays.stem: Explain the difference between qualifying an OFW procedure (PQR) and qualifying a welder (WPQ), and describe what each test involves.
essays.modelAnswer: A procedure qualification proves that the WPS itself can make a sound weld. A skilled welder makes a test coupon using set values, and every real value used, such as the rod, nozzle, flame, position and thickness, is written on the PQR. The coupon is inspected, then tested, usually with tensile tests across the weld and bend tests. If it passes, the WPS can be written from the PQR and used in production. A welder qualification proves that a person can follow an approved WPS. The welder makes a coupon in the test position. It is inspected by eye, then bend tested, or tested another way the code allows. If it passes, the results go on the WPQ, which states the process, positions, metal and thickness range the welder may now weld. One test proves the method; the other proves the person.
markingPoints: PQR proves the procedure can make a sound weld
Real values recorded; tensile and bend tests
WPQ proves the welder can follow the WPS
Welder test: visual, then bend tests or other code test
WPQ states the range the welder is qualified for

essays.stem: Describe how you would weld a 3G (vertical up) butt coupon in carbon steel plate with OFW to a WPS, from fit-up to the final run.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the WPS for the plate thickness, joint, gap, rod, nozzle and flame. I clean the joint area to bright metal on both sides. I set the gap with a gauge and tack each end with small, fully fused tacks, then check the gap and alignment. I clamp the coupon upright at a comfortable height, with the marked face towards me. I fit the nozzle from the maker's chart, set the pressures, light up and adjust to a neutral flame. I start at the bottom, make a small pool that melts both edges and the root, then add rod at the front edge of the pool. I travel upward with the flame angled up, so the pool sits on the weld below and does not sag. I keep the inner cone just clear of the pool and the rod inside the flame. At the top I fill the crater and draw the flame away slowly. Then I check both sides.
markingPoints: Reads WPS; cleans; sets gap and fused tacks
Correct nozzle and neutral flame
Starts at the bottom, melts both edges and root
Travels upward, controls pool, cone clear, rod in flame
Fills crater, cools slowly, checks both sides

essays.stem: Describe how you would weld a small-bore carbon steel pipe coupon in the 6G position with OFW, including the tacks, the order of welding round the pipe and the tie-ins.
essays.modelAnswer: I check the WPS for the pipe size, wall, joint, rod and nozzle, and clean the ends inside and out. I set the gap and line up the pipes, then tack at three or four points, keeping the tacks small and away from the bottom where I will start. I fix the coupon at 45° at the height the test sets and mark the top. I set a neutral flame. The weld is made in two halves. I start just past the bottom centre and weld uphill on one side to just past the top, keeping a small pool that fuses the root all round. I change my body and torch angle as I move from overhead to vertical to flat. For the second half I reheat the start of the first half at the bottom and fuse into it, then weld up the other side and fuse into the end of the first half at the top. I fill the crater and check the inside root.
markingPoints: Reads WPS; cleans ends; sets gap and tacks clear of the start
Fixes coupon at 45°; neutral flame
Two halves, each from bottom to top
Changes angles through overhead, vertical and flat
Fused tie-ins at bottom and top; fills crater; checks root

essays.stem: Compare forehand (leftward) and backhand (rightward) gas welding for a qualification test, and explain how the WPS decides which is used.
essays.modelAnswer: In forehand welding the flame points ahead, onto the cold metal, and the rod is fed in front of the flame. It preheats the joint, gives a small, flat bead and suits thin sheet, up to about 6 mm, where burn-through is the main risk. On thicker metal it needs a wide V, uses more rod and gas, and the root can be poorly fused. In backhand welding the flame points back over the weld just made, with the rod between the flame and the weld. The heat goes into the pool and the root, so it fuses thicker metal with a narrower V, and the flame shields the hot weld. It is often used on pipe walls and plate over about 6 mm. The WPS names the technique because it was proved on the PQR. The welder must use the technique the WPS gives in the test, since a change may change the result.
markingPoints: Forehand: flame ahead, rod in front; suits thin sheet
Forehand limits on thick metal
Backhand: flame over the weld; deeper fusion, narrower V
Backhand suits thicker plate and pipe
WPS sets the technique as proved; welder must follow it

essays.stem: Explain how face and root bend strips are taken, prepared and judged for an OFW test coupon, and what happens if a strip fails.
essays.modelAnswer: First the coupon must pass visual inspection. The strips are then marked out across the weld from the places the code sets, so that the hardest parts are tested. They are cut by saw or machine, not by flame near the weld. The face and root are ground or machined flush with the plate along the strip, and the long edges are rounded a little so that saw marks do not start cracks. Each strip is marked so it can be traced to the welder and the coupon. A face bend is bent with the cap side outside; a root bend with the root side outside. Each is bent in a guided bend jig round a former of the size the code gives. The outside of the bend is then checked for open defects and measured against the code's limits. If a strip fails, the welder fails that test. A retest is allowed only as the code sets out, often after more training.
markingPoints: Visual first; strips from set places
Cut by saw or machine; dressed flush; edges rounded; marked
Face and root bends explained
Bent in a guided jig and judged against code limits
Fail means retest only under the code's rules

essays.stem: Describe four defects that make OFW test coupons fail, such as lack of root fusion, porosity, burnt weld metal and crater cracks. Give a cause and a cure for each.
essays.modelAnswer: Lack of root fusion is often caused by too small a gap, too small a nozzle, or travelling too fast so the root edges never melt. The cure is to fit up to the WPS, use the right nozzle and watch both edges melt before adding rod. Porosity can come from dirty rod or plate, or from lifting the flame away so the pool is left bare to the air. The cure is to clean to bright metal, keep rods dry and keep the outer envelope over the pool. Burnt, oxidised weld metal, with heavy sparking, comes from an oxidising flame. The cure is to reset to neutral and check it during the weld. Crater cracks come from stopping suddenly and leaving an unfilled crater. The cure is to fill the crater with rod and draw the flame away slowly so it cools gently.
markingPoints: Lack of root fusion: cause and cure
Porosity: cause and cure
Burnt or oxidised weld: cause and cure
Crater cracks: cause and cure
Causes and cures are correct and match

essays.stem: Describe how you would set up and run a safe OFW test bay for six trainees, covering the cylinders, equipment checks, ventilation, fire and burns.
essays.modelAnswer: Cylinders are chained upright on trolleys or a wall, away from heat, with acetylene cylinders stood upright for the time the supplier says before use. Spares are stored outside in a ventilated store. Before use each set is checked: regulators, hoses, flashback arrestors at the regulators and check valves at the torch, with a leak test using a proper solution. Faulty parts are tagged and taken out of use. The bay has good ventilation or fume extraction, and oxygen is never used to freshen the air. Benches are steel or firebrick, the floor is clear of rubbish and oil, and an extinguisher is close by. Trainees wear goggles of the right shade, flame-resistant clothes, gloves and boots. Hot coupons are quenched or marked HOT and handled with tongs. At the end, cylinder valves are closed, lines bled and the bay checked for fire.
markingPoints: Cylinders upright, secured and stored correctly
Daily set checks, arrestors, check valves, leak test
Ventilation; no oxygen for fresh air
Fire control: clear area, firebrick bench, extinguisher
PPE, hot work marked, shut-down and fire check

essays.stem: Explain what records are kept for an OFW qualification test, from marking the coupon to issuing the WPQ, and why each one matters.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the test the coupon is stamped or marked with the welder's identity, the test number and the position, so it cannot be swapped. The WPS used is named on the test sheet. During the test the assessor records the real values, such as nozzle, rod, flame and position, and notes the times and any stops. The visual inspection result is written down with any faults. Each bend strip is marked so it is traced to the coupon, and the result of each bend is recorded with any defect sizes. If the welder passes, a WPQ is issued stating the process, positions, metal and thickness range. After that a continuity log shows the welder keeps using the process, so the qualification stays in force. These records prove the test was fair and traceable, and they show a client or inspector who may weld which joints.
markingPoints: Coupon marked to welder, test and position
WPS named and real values recorded
Visual and bend results recorded and traced
WPQ states the range; continuity log kept
Records prove fairness and show who may weld what

essays.stem: As team leader, explain how you would prepare a group of trainees for an OFW qualification test and run the test day fairly.
essays.modelAnswer: Some weeks before, I give each trainee the WPS and explain every detail: joint, rod, nozzle, flame, position and technique. I set practice coupons in the test position and cut and bend some, so trainees see their own faults and learn the code's limits. On the day, I check every gas set, arrestor and hose and the ventilation, and brief the safety rules. Each trainee gets a stamped coupon and the same materials and time. I watch fit-up and welding to make sure the WPS and position are followed, but I do not help. I inspect each coupon by eye against the code, then strips are cut from the set places, bent and judged the same way for all. I record every result honestly and explain them to each trainee. A trainee who fails gets feedback and a retest only as the code allows.
markingPoints: Briefs the WPS and the code's acceptance limits
Practice coupons with feedback
Safe set-up and same conditions for all
Watches without helping; tests and judges consistently
Honest records, feedback and code retest rules

practical1.title: OFW vertical-up (3G) butt coupons in carbon steel plate to a WPS, with visual inspection, face and root bends and a draft WPQ
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a WPS for oxy-acetylene welding of a butt joint in carbon steel plate (about 3 mm, or as the WPS says) in the 3G position, welded uphill. First, as a group, read the WPS and fill in the top of the group's test record: rod class and size, nozzle, flame, gap and technique. Each member then cleans, sets the gap and tacks one coupon (two plates about 150 mm × 75 mm), clamps it upright and welds it to the WPS. The assessor marks each coupon with the member's number before tacking. When the coupons are cool, members swap and inspect another member's coupon by eye on both sides (fusion, root penetration, undercut, cracks, crater) and record it. Coupons that pass are cut by the assessor into face and root bend strips. Members dress the strips, the assessor bends them in the jig, and the group judges and records each one against the limits the assessor gives. Finally each member fills in a draft WPQ for their own result. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the test record and the draft WPQs once for the whole group.
materials: Carbon steel plate coupons, about 3 mm × 150 mm × 75 mm, two per member, plus practice pieces
AWS-class steel gas welding rod as the WPS gives (for example R60), about 2.4 mm
Oxy-acetylene sets with flashback arrestors and check valves, one per booth
Nozzles and the maker's nozzle chart; spark lighter; tip cleaners
Vertical coupon clamp or positioner; gap gauge; wire brush; file or grinder
Saw and guided bend jig (used by the assessor), files to dress strips
WPS, test record sheet and blank WPQ forms (from the assessor)
photos: The WPS and the group's test record with settings filled in
One coupon tacked, with the gap gauge in place and the coupon number showing
A member welding uphill in the 3G position
Face and root sides of every finished coupon
Bend strips after bending, laid out by coupon number
The completed test record and draft WPQs
checklist: Read the WPS and set the nozzle, flame and gap it gives
Cleaned the joint and tacked with small, fused tacks
Welded uphill in the 3G position with a controlled pool and full root
Kept a neutral flame and filled the crater at the end
Inspected another member's coupon and recorded faults correctly
Judged the bend strips against the limits given and filled in a correct WPQ
Worked safely: PPE, torch handling, hot work marked
safety: Check arrestors, hoses and regulators and leak-test each set before lighting
Wear gas welding goggles of the right shade, flame-resistant clothes and gloves
Keep the bay ventilated; never use oxygen to freshen the air
Quench or mark hot coupons HOT and handle them with tongs
Only the assessor uses the saw and the bend jig; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: OFW small-bore carbon steel pipe coupons in the 6G position, with a PQR-style record of real values and bend tests
practical2.brief: The assessor gives your group a draft WPS for gas welding small-bore carbon steel pipe (about 50–60 mm outside diameter, wall about 3–4 mm) in the 6G position (pipe fixed at 45°). If the assessor decides, a member may weld 5G (pipe fixed horizontal) instead. Share the roles: one member is the recorder, who writes down the real values each welder uses (nozzle, pressures, rod, flame, position, start and stop times) on a PQR-style record; every member, including the recorder, welds one coupon. Each member cleans the pipe ends inside and out, sets the gap, tacks clear of the start point, fixes the coupon at 45° and welds it in two halves from bottom to top with fused tie-ins. Members inspect each other's coupons outside and inside (with a mirror or after cutting) and record what they find. The assessor cuts bend strips from the places the code sets on two coupons; the group dresses, bends (with the assessor) and judges them. Finally, the group compares the real values with the draft WPS and writes three lines saying whether the WPS needs changing. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the PQR-style record, inspection notes and the comparison once for the whole group.
materials: Carbon steel pipe pieces, about 50–60 mm OD, cut and bevelled as the WPS gives, two per member
Steel gas welding rod of the class and size the WPS gives
Oxy-acetylene sets with flashback arrestors and check valves; nozzles and the maker's chart
Pipe stand or positioner that fixes the coupon at 45°; gap gauge; mirror; paint marker
Saw and guided bend jig (used by the assessor); files and grinder to dress strips
Draft WPS, PQR-style record sheet and inspection sheet (from the assessor)
photos: The draft WPS and the recorder's sheet at the start
A coupon tacked, with the start point and top marked
A coupon fixed at 45° in the stand, with a member welding the bottom half
The finished cap round one coupon, and the inside root seen with a mirror
Bend strips from two coupons after bending
The completed record and the group's comparison with the WPS
checklist: Cleaned the pipe ends inside and out and set the gap to the WPS
Tacked clear of the start and fixed the coupon at 45° (or 5G if directed)
Welded each half from bottom to top, changing angles round the pipe
Made fused tie-ins at the bottom and the top with no open crater
Recorded real values or inspection results accurately
Took part in judging the bends and comparing the values with the WPS
Worked safely throughout and left the bay clean and safe
safety: Check and leak-test each set before lighting; shut down and bleed lines after use
Keep the stand stable and the coupon secure before welding overhead parts
Wear goggles, flame-resistant clothes, gloves and a cap when welding under the pipe
Mark hot coupons HOT; quench or cool them in the set place
Keep the bay ventilated with an extinguisher close; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
